title: Analysis of Modified Plant Metabolites Using Widely Targeted Metabolite Modificomics
author: Jianing Zhang

materials: Tomato (MicroTom) seeds were surface sterilized at 50 °C for 30 min, germinated on moist filter paper in Petri dishes for two days, and then sown into trays filled with nursery soil. After five weeks, seedlings were transplanted into pots awaiting sampling or further treatment and planted at a density of 16.5 cm between plants in a row and 26 cm apart. Greenhouse management, including irrigation, fertilization, and pest control, essentially followed normal agricultural practices. Reagents

steps.title: Prepare extraction and LC solvents
steps.instruction: Make three solvent solutions: (1) 70 % methanol extraction solvent (1 L) by mixing 700 mL HPLC‑grade methanol, 300 mL deionized water and lidocaine (Sigma‑Aldrich L1026) to a final concentration of 1 mg L⁻¹; store at 4 °C. (2) LC solvent A (1 L) by adding 0.4 mL HPLC‑grade acetic acid (Merck 5.43808.0100) to 1 000 mL deionized water; prepare before use. (3) LC solvent B (1 L) by adding 0.4 mL HPLC‑grade acetic acid to 1 000 mL HPLC‑grade acetonitrile (Merck 1.00029.2500); prepare before use.

steps.title: Select and harvest tomato plants
steps.instruction: Randomly choose nine MicroTom tomato plants with uniform growth, group every three plants as one biological replicate (total three replicates), cut leaves and roots and place them into 50 mL centrifuge tubes equipped with holes, then immediately freeze the samples in liquid nitrogen; if freeze‑drying cannot start right away, store tubes at –80 °C.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry and grind plant material
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry the harvested samples for 7 days, then grind the dried tissue in an MM400 grinder at 25 Hz for 1.5 min; keep the resulting powder at –80 °C until extraction.

steps.title: Extract metabolites with 70 % methanol
steps.instruction: Pre‑chill the 70 % methanol extraction solvent at 4 °C. Weigh 0.1 g of freeze‑dried powder into a 2 mL screw‑top centrifuge tube (Agilent 5182‑0716), add 1 mL of the chilled solvent (ratio 1 mL g⁻¹), seal, vortex at maximum speed, place on ice for 10 min, vortex again; repeat vortex‑ice cycle three times total, then store the tube at 4 °C for 10 h.

steps.title: Centrifuge, filter, and store extracts
steps.instruction: After the 10 h incubation, vortex the tubes, pre‑cool a centrifuge to 4 °C and spin at 10 000 × g for 10 min. Transfer the supernatant to a new tube, filter through a 0.2 µm Captiva syringe filter (Agilent 5190‑5269) using a 2 mL disposable syringe (Agilent 5610‑2111), collect the filtrate in 2 mL glass inserts (Agilent 5183‑2088) placed in 2 mL screw‑top vials (Agilent 5182‑0716), and store at –80 °C. Vortex thoroughly before LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Prepare quality‑control samples
steps.instruction: Create a blank QC by filling a vial with methanol only, and a pooled QC by mixing equal volumes of all extracted samples; insert these blanks and pooled QCs periodically during the LC‑MS run to monitor background and instrument stability.

steps.title: Set up UHPLC gradient run
steps.instruction: Install a Shim‑pack GISS C18 column (2 × 150 mm, 5 µm; Shimadzu catalog 227‑30066‑03) on the Shimadzu Nexera X2 system, set column temperature to 40 °C, and use an injection volume of 2 µL. Load mobile phase A (water + 0.04 % acetic acid) and mobile phase B (acetonitrile + 0.04 % acetic acid). Program the gradient at a flow rate of 0.4 mL min⁻¹ as follows: 0 min 95 % A/5 % B; 5 min 5 % A/95 % B; 10 min 5 % A/95 % B; 11 min 95 % A/5 % B; 11.1 min 95 % A/5 % B; 15 min 95 % A/5 % B.

steps.title: Acquire NL‑IDA‑EPI data on Q‑Trap
steps.instruction: Run the extracts on an API 6500 Q‑Trap LC‑MS/MS in NL‑IDA‑EPI mode. Set ESI source temperature to 500 °C, ion spray voltage to 5500 V, gas I = 55 psi, gas II = 60 psi, curtain gas = 25 psi, and collision gas to high mode. Program a neutral‑loss scan from 14 Da to 245 Da in 1 Da steps; set precursor ion scan range to 19–1000 Da. When a preset NL is detected with sufficient intensity, trigger IDA to acquire enhanced product ion (EPI) spectra.

steps.title: Acquire high‑resolution data on Orbitrap
steps.instruction: Analyze the same extracts on a Q Exactive Plus Orbitrap in full MS/dd‑MS2 mode with a precursor range of 50–1000 Da. Set sheath gas to 40 psi, auxiliary gas to 12 psi, spray voltage to 3000 V, capillary temperature to 360 °C, S‑lens voltage to 55 V, and auxiliary gas heater temperature to 350 °C.

steps.title: Process NL‑IDA‑EPI data
steps.instruction: Collect Q1 (precursor) and Q3 (product) information, including all fragment ions, retention times, and intensities. Remove duplicate entries (same precursor, product, RT) and discard signals with signal‑to‑noise ratio < 10 to generate a preliminary metabolic‑signal dataset.

steps.title: Process Orbitrap high‑resolution data
steps.instruction: Integrate the Orbitrap data with the Q‑Trap dataset, align Q1, Q3, and RT values, deduplicate, and build a high‑quality tomato metabolite modificomics MS2T database containing high‑resolution precursor and product ion information.

steps.title: Identify neutral losses with MS2Analyzer
steps.instruction: Load the MS2T dataset into MS2Analyzer software to automatically detect neutral losses, then compare the m/z, RT, fragment patterns, and NL types with standard spectral libraries, commercial databases, and literature; for metabolites lacking standards, use Compound Discoverer 3.1 for database matching and perform manual annotation as needed.

steps.title: Build WTMM database via MetDNA
steps.instruction: Import identified metabolites into MetDNA, apply recursive algorithms based on metabolic reaction networks to discover unknown metabolites, and compile the results into the tomato widely‑targeted metabolite modificomics (WTMM) database.

steps.title: Optimize MRM transitions and parameters
steps.instruction: Select a precursor ion (e.g., m/z 476.3 Da) and two high‑abundance product ions (e.g., 335.1 and 304.1 Da) from the MS2T library to form ion pairs 476.3/335.1 and 476.3/304.1. Perform scheduled MRM on the Q‑Trap, testing declustering potential (DP) and collision energy (CE) at 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 V in all 36 combinations. Remove peaks with poor shape, low intensity, low SNR, or excessively high intensity; retain high‑quality peaks and record the optimal DP/CE settings for future analyses.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research article: Yang et al. [6]. A widely targeted metabolite modificomics strategy for modified metabolites identification in tomato. JIPB.
